svg.aria-label: How to write नाम: 5 strokes · 4 pen lifts · 7 movements
svg.title: Writing नाम
svg.desc: 7 frames; frame N shows movements 1 to N of नाम (devanagari): each letter's body in reading order, then one headline over the whole word; the movement being added is drawn in ink over the finished word, whose outline (each letter's at the font's advance) is read from _fonts/NotoSansDevanagari-Static.ttf. Stroke order after letter 1: Opiaterein, ‘Deva-न-order.gif’, strokes 1–3, Wikimedia Commons, 11 May 2009; sign 2: HP Labs India, Lipi Toolkit, Lipi Indic Character Recognizers 4.0, Devanagari recognizer, class 47 (ा, aa sign): stored online-handwriting prototypes from native writers (MIT licence, 2012); letter 3: JackPotte, ‘Devanagari m म.gif’, strokes 1–3, Wikimedia Commons, 29 March 2009; the place of sign 2, after its consonant's body: Saurmandal, ‘Devanagari आ stroke order.svg’, frames 1–5, Wikimedia Commons, 5 August 2023; the shared headline, drawn last: HP Labs India, Lipi Toolkit, Lipi Indic Character Recognizers 4.0, Devanagari recognizer: native writers' stored prototypes of the 33 consonants draw the headline as the last stroke in 82% of 2,706 and as the first in about 5% (MIT licence, 2012) <https://lipitk.sourceforge.net/lipi-reco.htm>. Source note on variation: The letters are drawn in reading order, each as its own cited strip draws it but without its own headline, placed where the bundled font prints it in the word: letter 1 after Opiaterein, ‘Deva-न-order.gif’, strokes 1–3, Wikimedia Commons, 11 May 2009 <https://commons.wikimedia.org/wiki/File:Deva-%E0%A4%A8-order.gif>; sign 2 after HP Labs India, Lipi Toolkit, Lipi Indic Character Recognizers 4.0, Devanagari recognizer, class 47 (ा, aa sign): stored online-handwriting prototypes from native writers (MIT licence, 2012) <https://lipitk.sourceforge.net/lipi-reco.htm>; letter 3 after JackPotte, ‘Devanagari m म.gif’, strokes 1–3, Wikimedia Commons, 29 March 2009 <https://commons.wikimedia.org/wiki/File:Devanagari_m_%E0%A4%AE.gif>. Each letter's own note on variation is printed with that letter's own strip. The place of sign 2, after its consonant's body and before the headline, after Saurmandal, ‘Devanagari आ stroke order.svg’, frames 1–5, Wikimedia Commons, 5 August 2023 <https://commons.wikimedia.org/wiki/File:Devanagari_%E0%A4%86_stroke_order.svg>; the sign's own piece of headline becomes part of the word's one headline. The cited आ is अ with the ā bar after it: its buildup frames draw the body, then (frame 4) the trailing stem top-to-bottom, then (frame 5) the shirorekhā left-to-right. The book draws the ā sign the same way on a consonant: the consonant's body, then the stem, then the headline across both. Native writers agree for आ: of the 83 prototypes of आ stored in HP Labs India's LipiTk 4.0 Devanagari recognizer, 52 (63%) are body strokes, then the bar, then the headline; the bar comes after the body in 69% and before the headline in 65% (the data is licensed for research use only, so only shares are cited). KanoAI's hand-made Gujarati barakhadi templates draw ા after its consonant in all 32 rows that keep the consonant's bare outline, in a script with no headline. No reachable source records native writers' consonant + ā syllables (HP Labs India's hpl-dvng-iso-word set, which would, is on a host the authoring environment cannot reach), so carrying आ's order to the sign on a consonant is this book's reading of that evidence, at medium confidence. Handwriting varies by writer. The headline is then drawn once, left to right, over the whole word. That is the order most native writers use for a single letter: in HP Labs India's LipiTk 4.0 Devanagari recognizer the stored prototypes of the 33 consonants draw the headline last in 82% of 2,706 and first in about 5%. It is a majority, not a rule: some writers draw the headline first. The traces are single letters, so carrying their order across a word is this book's reading of them; no reachable source records native writers' headline timing in whole words.
svg.text: How it is written — 5 strokes · 4 pen lifts · 7 movements
Stroke order after letter 1: Opiaterein, ‘Deva-न-order.gif’, strokes 1–3, Wikimedia Commons, 11 May 2009; sign 2: HP Labs India, Lipi Toolkit, Lipi Indic Character Recognizers 4.0,
Devanagari recognizer, class 47 (ा, aa sign): stored online-handwriting prototypes from native writers (MIT licence, 2012); letter 3: JackPotte, ‘Devanagari m म.gif’, strokes 1–3,
Wikimedia Commons, 29 March 2009; the place of sign 2, after its consonant's body: Saurmandal, ‘Devanagari आ stroke order.svg’, frames 1–5, Wikimedia Commons, 5 August 2023; the
shared headline, drawn last: HP Labs India, Lipi Toolkit, Lipi Indic Character Recognizers 4.0, Devanagari recognizer: native writers' stored prototypes of the 33 consonants draw the
headline as the last stroke in 82% of 2,706 and as the first in about 5% (MIT licence, 2012)
This order is attested, not standardised; the source records where it varies.
